:::{#thm-pderiv-normal-parameters}
#### Partial derivatives of the normal density with respect to its parameters

Let $\mean \in \reals$ and $\sdpar > 0$, and let

$$f(x; \mean, \sdpar) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sdpar^2}}\expf{-\frac{(x - \mean)^2}{2\sdpar^2}}$$

Then for every $x \in \reals$,

$$
\ba
\derivf{f}{\mean} &= \frac{x - \mean}{\sdpar^2} f(x; \mean, \sdpar)
\\
\derivf{f}{\sdpar} &= \sb{-\frac{1}{\sdpar} + \frac{(x - \mean)^2}{\sdpar^3}} f(x; \mean, \sdpar)
\ea
$$

:::

::: proof

This is the solution to @exr-miller-pderiv-normal-parameters.

:::
